title: Elon Musk Admits to Throttling Ukraine's Starlink, Citing Terms of Service Violations
snippet: Tech billionaire Elon Musk acknowledged that SpaceX intentionally restricted Starlink satellite speeds in Ukraine, claiming the military violated service terms by using the civilian network for offensive drone strikes.
content:
WASHINGTON — Tech mogul Elon Musk confirmed Saturday that SpaceX intentionally throttled its Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, taking responsibility for disruptions that hampered Ukrainian military operations for more than a week.

Musk’s public admission on X (formerly Twitter) followed announcements from Ukrainian officials that internet connectivity had finally been restored to operational speeds. The decision to curb connectivity underscored the complex reliance of Kyiv's defense forces on private commercial technology provided by the American billionaire.

Terms of Service Dispute

Addressing the restrictions, Musk maintained that the service was never meant to be weaponized. “Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” Musk posted, asserting that Ukrainian forces violated terms of service and that SpaceX moved to close a technical loophole.

However, Musk clarified that the U.S. government maintains control over modifications to Starshield, the military-grade variant of the satellite network heavily utilized for command, communications, and drone warfare. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Saturday morning that service speeds had returned to required levels, bolstering front-line logistics and counter-drone defense systems.

Political Strain in Washington and Kyiv

The throttling incident triggered friction between Kyiv and Washington, raising concerns among Ukrainian commanders who reported compromised operations and lost tactical assets. The episode comes amid mixed signals from the White House regarding official involvement.

While President Donald Trump denied ordering the slowdown and defended Musk, Vice President JD Vance hinted at administrative coordination. Meanwhile, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth rejected claims of White House participation in the private firm's decisions. Tensions remain elevated following recent diplomatic maneuvers, including a localized ceasefire brokered near Oleshky and upcoming trilateral peace talks involving Washington, Kyiv, and Moscow.

War Escalates Across Frontlines

Despite brief diplomatic breakthroughs, combat operations show no sign of stopping. A Russian missile attack struck Lozova in the Kharkiv region on Saturday, leaving one dead and two injured. Meanwhile, Russian-occupied Crimea experienced widespread power outages following sustained overnight strikes by Ukrainian forces.

Kyiv also demonstrated expanding long-range strike capabilities, targeting industrial assets deep inside Russian territory. Ukrainian drones hit a chemical plant in Tolyatti, an electronics facility supplying missile components in Oryol, and an industrial center in Omsk, Siberia—located more than 1,200 miles from the Ukrainian border.
